Getting Around
PassApp
Foreign number: accepted — the app takes a foreign country code at sign-up, but the verification SMS does not always reach a foreign carrier; a local SIM avoids the issue.
The Cambodian-born app locals default to, with fixed fares and no haggling; it usually comes out cheaper than Grab for the same tuk-tuk or car route around town.
passapp.info
Grab
Foreign number: accepted — the app takes a foreign country code at sign-up, but the verification SMS does not always reach a foreign carrier; a local SIM avoids the issue.
The Southeast Asian super-app, running 20 to 50 percent pricier than PassApp on the same local route, but the same account works across Thailand, Vietnam and other border crossings.
grab.com
Worth Knowing

The Angkor Pass has three tiers, and the 3-day option is the one built for a trip this length

The official Angkor Pass, sold only through Angkor Enterprise, comes in three tiers: a 1-day pass for US$37, a 3-day pass for US$62 that stays valid across any 7 days from first use, and a 7-day pass for US$72 valid across any 30 days. Temple entry opens at 5:00am and the park closes at 6:30pm. A passport photo is taken on-site for the pass, so there is no need to bring one, and the physical card doubles as the ticket at every gate for its whole validity window.

Buying the pass a day ahead removes the single biggest risk to a sunrise visit: showing up at 4:45am to find the ticket line still moving. The 3-day tier fits this itinerary's Angkor-heavy days with room to spare if a sunrise gets clouded out and is worth retrying.

Riel and US dollars circulate side by side in Siem Reap, and prices under a dollar are settled in riel as small change — ATMs across town dispense dollars, not riel. Carrying riel on purpose is unnecessary; it arrives as change and spends the same as a dollar bill everywhere it is handed over.
